plan.title: Psoriasis lesional vs control hallmark GSEA
plan.analytical_narrative: The research question asks which hallmark pathways change between psoriasis-lesional and control skin. DE is already done (DESeq2 results table, treated=lesional vs control, 12000 genes). Because raw counts and metadata are also provided, we first run a lightweight sample-structure QC on the counts (blind VST + PCA + sample distance heatmap) to characterize sample_01's low library size (~4x below median) and confirm it does not distort the DE-derived ranking we are about to use — per knowledge-service rule R-0008/R-0030, we do not drop this sample silently, we only report it, since the DE has already been fit on it. We then take the delivered DESeq2 results table, rank the full tested gene list by the Wald statistic (stat column, not log2FC alone, not signed p-value with ties — R-0099/R-0108), and run fgsea preranked GSEA against the MSigDB Hallmark human gene set collection (2026.1, 50 sets) as the primary pass, with Reactome human pathways as a secondary collection to resolve any hallmark hit into specific pathways (R-0048/R-0098). Gene sets are filtered to the 15-500 member window intersected with the tested genes (R-0047), redundant significant sets are collapsed (R-0052), and the final report states the ranking metric, collection versions, universe, leading-edge genes per significant set, and the enrichment-method-dependence caveat (R-0051/R-0055/R-0105/R-0086).

steps.method: DESeq2 vst(blind) + PCA + sample distance heatmap on raw counts
fgsea preranked GSEA on DESeq2 Wald statistic vs MSigDB Hallmark, followed by Reactome as second collection
Enrichment report with leading edge genes, method-dependence caveat, reproducibility record
